ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The forest line is an important ecological boundary in the vertical natural belt spectrum of high mountains, usually referring to the upper limit of tree (coniferous forest) growth at high elevations. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows the distribution of altitude contour lines of alpine forest lines in a local region of China, marked with 80°E, 90°E, 100°E and latitude-longitude lines near 30°N; the values of the equal forest lines include 3800, 4000, 4200, 4400 meters, etc. In the eastern part of the figure, near about 100°E, multiple equal forest lines no longer maintain the relatively gentle nearly east-west extension in the west, but bend obviously, showing nearly north-south or arc-shaped turns, with a form similar to the extension direction of the eastern margin of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and the mountains in Southwest China. Then reason: If the trend of forest line altitude contour lines is consistent with the mountain range trend and the terrain edge height, it indicates that its spatial variation is first controlled by the topographic pattern. In the eastern region, the change in the trend of multiple forest lines mainly corresponds to the sharp change in terrain on the eastern margin of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and the turn of mountain range trends; therefore, the primary influencing factor is terrain and mountain range trend.

In the eastern region, the change in the trend of multiple forest lines mainly corresponds to the sharp change in terrain on the eastern margin of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and the turn of mountain range trends; therefore, the primary influencing factor is terrain and mountain range trend.
